title: Gujarat Father Arrested After Daughter, 21, Killed Over Inter-Caste Relationship
excerpt: Police in Anand district allege the father strangled his daughter with her dupatta on Diwali night and the death was presented as natural until a postmortem found ligature strangulation.
body:
• Police in Gujarat's Anand district say a 21-year-old woman, identified in reports as Sanya Patel, was killed by her father on Diwali night after an argument over her relationship with a man from another caste.
  • Police say the father strangled her with her dupatta and the death was initially presented as natural; a forensic postmortem found death by ligature strangulation.
  • Police say the accused confessed during questioning; he has been arrested and sent to judicial custody.
  • All details are police allegations at this stage — the case has not been tried.

A 21-year-old woman in Gujarat's Anand district was killed on Diwali night, allegedly by her own father, after an argument over her relationship with a man from another caste, according to police accounts reported by the Press Trust of India and carried by The Indian Express and Rediff. The woman was identified in news reports as Sanya Patel, of Metpur village in the Khambhat area of Anand district.

What police say happened

According to the police account carried in those reports, an argument broke out between the father and daughter on the night of Diwali over the relationship. Police allege the father strangled her with her own dupatta. The death was initially portrayed as natural, the reports say, but a forensic postmortem examination established the cause of death as ligature strangulation, which led police to question the family.

Arrest and custody

Police say the father confessed to the killing during interrogation. He has been arrested and sent to judicial custody, according to the reports. These are allegations recorded by police and reported by news agencies; no court has tested them, and the accused is entitled to the presumption of innocence. Police have not, in the reports available, published a detailed chargesheet, and further investigation details — including any statements from other family members — have not been made public in the coverage so far.

The wider pattern

Killings of young people, most often women, by family members opposed to an inter-caste or otherwise disapproved relationship are a recurring category of crime in India, tracked by the National Crime Records Bureau under murder statistics rather than any separate "honour crime" head. What distinguishes cases like this one in the official record is how rarely the initial account survives scrutiny: here, according to police, it was the postmortem finding — not a complaint — that converted a death presented as natural into a murder investigation. Readers following the case should expect the next verified developments to come from the chargesheet and the first court hearings in Anand district, not from further police briefings alone.
